celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَالطُّورِ﴾ that is, the mountain on which Allah spoke to Moses.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَكِتَابٍ مَسْطُورٍ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here; the gloss follows in the next entry.]

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿فِي رَقٍّ مَنْشُورٍ﴾ that is, the Torah or the Quran.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَالْبَيْتِ الْمَعْمُورِ﴾ It is in the third, or the sixth, or the seventh heaven, opposite the Kaaba; seventy thousand angels visit it every day for circumambulation and prayer, never returning to it again.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَالْبَحْرِ الْمَسْجُورِ﴾ that is, the filled one.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّكَ لَوَاقِعٌ﴾ will surely come down upon the one who deserves it;

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ governed (maʿmūl) by لَوَاقِعٌ; ﴿تَمُورُ السَّمَاءُ مَوْرًا﴾ it moves and revolves,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَتَسِيرُ الْجِبَالُ سَيْرًا﴾ they become scattered dust; and that is on the Day of Resurrection.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ﴾ severity of punishment ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ of the messengers,

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي خَوْضٍ﴾ of falsehood ﴿يَلْعَبُونَ﴾ that is, they occupy themselves with their disbelief.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلَى نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا﴾ they are pushed violently; a badal (substitute) for يَوْمَ تَمُورُ. And it is said to them, by way of reproach:

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿هَذِهِ النَّارُ الَّتِي كُنْتُمْ بِهَا تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾. [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿أَفَسِحْرٌ هَذَا﴾ — the punishment which you see — just as you used to say of the revelation "This is sorcery"? ﴿أَمْ أَنْتُمْ لَا تُبْصِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿اصْلَوْهَا فَاصْبِرُوا﴾ upon it ﴿أَوْ لَا تَصْبِرُوا﴾ your patience and your anguish are ﴿سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ because your patience will not benefit you; ﴿إِنَّمَا تُجْزَوْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ that is, the recompense of it.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَنَعِيمٍ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿فَاكِهِينَ﴾ delighting ﴿بِمَا﴾ maṣdariyya (the مَا that forms a maṣdar) ﴿آتَاهُمْ﴾ He has given them, ﴿رَبُّهُمْ وَوَقَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ عَذَابَ الْجَحِيمِ﴾ conjoined to آتَاهُمْ, that is: in His giving them and His protecting them. And it is said to them:

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, enjoying it wholesomely; ﴿بِمَا﴾ the bāʾ is causal; ﴿كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustakinn) pronoun in His words, Exalted is He, فِي جَنَّاتٍ; ﴿عَلَى سُرُرٍ مَصْفُوفَةٍ﴾ one beside the other; ﴿وَزَوَّجْنَاهُمْ﴾ conjoined to فِي جَنَّاتٍ, that is, We paired them ﴿بِحُورٍ عِينٍ﴾ large-eyed, beautiful ones.

celaleyn:21-21.t:
﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to آمَنُوا [وَأَتْبَعْنَاهُمْ] ﴿ذُرِّيَّاتُهُمْ﴾ the young and the old [ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ] ﴿بِإِيمَانٍ﴾ on the part of the older ones, and on the part of the fathers in the case of the young ones; and the khabar (predicate) is ﴿أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ﴾ those mentioned, in Paradise, so that they are in their rank even if they did not do as they did, as an honour to the fathers by gathering the children to them [ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ]; ﴿وَمَا أَلَتْنَاهُمْ﴾ with fatḥa and kasra on the lām: We did not diminish them ﴿مِنْ عَمَلِهِمْ مِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ to be added to the work of the children; ﴿كُلُّ امْرِئٍ بِمَا كَسَبَ﴾ of work, good or evil, ﴿رَهِينٌ﴾ pledged: he is held to account for evil and rewarded for good.
[Translator's note: the bracketed Arabic words are variant readings given in the source text.]

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَأَمْدَدْنَاهُمْ﴾ We increase them time after time ﴿بِفَاكِهَةٍ وَلَحْمٍ مِمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ﴾ even if they do not explicitly ask for it.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿يَتَنَازَعُونَ﴾ they pass among themselves ﴿فِيهَا﴾ that is, in Paradise, ﴿كَأْسًا﴾ wine; ﴿لَا لَغْوٌ فِيهَا﴾ that is, occurring among them because of drinking it, ﴿وَلَا تَأْثِيمٌ﴾ attaching to them through it, unlike the wine of this world.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ in service ﴿غِلْمَانٌ﴾ servants ﴿لَهُمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ﴾ in beauty and delicacy ﴿لُؤْلُؤٌ مَكْنُونٌ﴾ guarded in the shell, because in it it is more beautiful than elsewhere.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ﴾ they ask one another about what they used to be in and what they have attained, out of delight and in acknowledgement of the blessing.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ hinting at the cause of their attainment: ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا قَبْلُ فِي أَهْلِنَا﴾ in this world ﴿مُشْفِقِينَ﴾ fearful of Allah's punishment;

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿فَمَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا﴾ with forgiveness ﴿وَوَقَانَا عَذَابَ السَّمُومِ﴾ that is, the Fire, [so called] because it enters the pores. And they said, also as a hint:

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ that is, in this world, ﴿نَدْعُوهُ﴾ that is, we worshipped Him, affirming His oneness; ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ with kasra, as a resumptive clause, even though it gives a reason in meaning; and with fatḥa, giving a reason in wording; ﴿هُوَ الْبَرُّ﴾ the Beneficent, true to His promise, ﴿الرَّحِيمُ﴾ great in mercy.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿فَذَكِّرْ﴾ continue reminding the idolaters and do not turn back from it because of their saying to you "a soothsayer, a madman"; ﴿فَمَا أَنْتَ بِنِعْمَتِ رَبِّكَ﴾ that is, by His favour upon you, ﴿بِكَاهِنٍ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of مَا ﴿وَلَا مَجْنُونٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ (meaning: rather) ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ he is ﴿شَاعِرٌ نَتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ رَيْبَ الْمَنُونِ﴾ the vicissitudes of time, so that he perishes like other poets.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿قُلْ تَرَبَّصُوا﴾ my destruction, ﴿فَإِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُتَرَبِّصِينَ﴾ your destruction; and they were punished by the sword on the day of Badr. التَّرَبُّصُ means waiting.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿أَمْ تَأْمُرُهُمْ أَحْلَامُهُمْ﴾ their minds ﴿بِهَذَا﴾ that is, their saying of him "a sorcerer, a soothsayer, a poet, a madman"? That is, they do not command them to do so. ﴿أَمْ﴾ (meaning: rather) ﴿هُمْ قَوْمٌ طَاغُونَ﴾ in their obstinacy.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ تَقَوَّلَهُ﴾ he invented the Quran? He did not invent it; ﴿بَلْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ out of arrogance. If they say he invented it,

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿فَلْيَأْتُوا بِحَدِيثٍ﴾ invented ﴿مِثْلِهِ إِنْ كَانُوا صَادِقِينَ﴾ in what they say.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿أَمْ خُلِقُوا مِنْ غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ﴾ that is, without a creator, ﴿أَمْ هُمُ الْخَالِقُونَ﴾ of themselves? A created thing without a creator is inconceivable, and a non-existent thing does not create; so they must have a Creator, and He is Allah the One. Why then do they not affirm His oneness and believe in His Messenger and His Book?

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿أَمْ خَلَقُوا السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ None is able to create them but Allah the Creator; why then do they not worship Him? ﴿بَلْ لَا يُوقِنُونَ﴾ in Him; otherwise they would have believed in His Prophet.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿أَمْ عِنْدَهُمْ خَزَائِنُ رَبِّكَ﴾ of prophethood, provision and other things, so that they may single out whomever they wish with whatever they wish? ﴿أَمْ هُمُ الْمُسَيْطِرُونَ﴾ the overpowering tyrants? Its verb is سَيْطَرَ, and like it are بَيْطَرَ and بَيْقَرَ.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿أَمْ لَهُمْ سُلَّمٌ﴾ a means of ascent to heaven, ﴿يَسْتَمِعُونَ فِيهِ﴾ that is, on it, to the speech of the angels, so that they could dispute with the Prophet, as they claim, if they claim that? ﴿فَلْيَأْتِ مُسْتَمِعُهُمْ﴾ that is, the one claiming to listen on it, ﴿بِسُلْطَانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ with a clear, evident proof. And because this claim resembles their claim that the angels are the daughters of Allah, He, Exalted is He, said:

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿أَمْ لَهُ الْبَنَاتُ﴾ that is, by your claim, ﴿وَلَكُمُ الْبَنُونَ﴾? Allah is far above what they claim.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿أَمْ تَسْأَلُهُمْ أَجْرًا﴾ for the religion you have brought them, ﴿فَهُمْ مِنْ مَغْرَمٍ﴾ the cost of that ﴿مُثْقَلُونَ﴾ so that they do not submit?

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿أَمْ عِنْدَهُمُ الْغَيْبُ﴾ that is, knowledge of it, ﴿فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ﴾ that, so that they could dispute with the Prophet ﷺ about the resurrection and the matters of the Hereafter, as they claim?

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿أَمْ يُرِيدُونَ كَيْدًا﴾ against you, to destroy you in Dār al-Nadwa? ﴿فَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هُمُ الْمَكِيدُونَ﴾ the overcome, the destroyed; so Allah protected him from them, then destroyed them at Badr.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿أَمْ لَهُمْ إِلَهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ with Him of gods. The interrogative with أَمْ in its places [here] is for denouncing and rebuking.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿وَإِنْ يَرَوْا كِسْفًا﴾ a part ﴿مِنَ السَّمَاءِ سَاقِطًا﴾ upon them, as they said {فَأَسْقِطْ عَلَيْنَا كِسْفًا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ}, that is, as a punishment for them, ﴿يَقُولُوا﴾ this is ﴿سَحَابٌ مَرْكُومٌ﴾ piled up, by which we will be watered; and they would not believe.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿فَذَرْهُمْ حَتَّى يُلَاقُوا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي فِيهِ يُصْعَقُونَ﴾ they die,

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿يَوْمَ لَا يُغْنِي﴾ a badal (substitute) for يَوْمَهُمْ ﴿عَنْهُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئًا وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ protected from the punishment in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾ by their disbelief ﴿عَذَابًا دُونَ ذَلِكَ﴾ that is, in this world before their death; so they were punished with hunger and drought for seven years, and with killing on the day of Badr; ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that the punishment will descend on them.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ﴾ in granting them respite, and let your breast not be constricted; ﴿فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا﴾ within Our sight: We see you and protect you; ﴿وَسَبِّحْ﴾ accompanied ﴿بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ﴾ that is, say «سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ», ﴿حِينَ تَقُومُ﴾ from your sleep or from your sitting.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ﴾ literally, as well; ﴿وَإِدْبَارَ النُّجُومِ﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun), that is, after their setting, glorify Him too; or [it means] pray: in the first, the two evening prayers (ʿishāʾayn), and in the second, the dawn prayer (fajr); and it is said: the morning prayer (ṣubḥ).
